drhp.business: Alufluoride Limited manufactures aluminium fluoride (AlF3), a specialty fluorine chemical used as a flux by primary aluminium smelters in the electrolytic reduction of alumina, converting hydro-fluosilicic acid (FSA) - a byproduct of phosphatic fertiliser manufacture - into high-purity AlF3 for smelter customers across India. Alongside this single product line, the Company runs a small captive solar power generation activity, used mainly for captive consumption with surplus units sold to the grid.
drhp.end_markets: Indian primary aluminium smelters (domestic market; no export sales registered in the current or previous year)
drhp.expansion: The Company has expanded its AlF3 manufacturing capacity at Visakhapatnam in phases: 4,000 TPA at commissioning; 8,000 TPA through debottlenecking over the years; 12,000 TPA in a second phase; 18,000 TPA in a subsequent debottlenecking; and 24,000 TPA on completion of the final phase in June 2026. A further expansion of AlF3 production infrastructure, undertaken in anticipation of increased FSA (raw material) availability, was targeted for completion by end of June 2026 and is stated to give the enhanced facility a production capacity of 80 tons per day (TPD). risks.note: FSA, the Company's key raw material, is sourced principally from IFFCO Paradeep and supplemented by Paradeep Phosphates and Coromandel International's phosphoric acid plants; all suppliers ultimately depend on imported rock phosphate, sulphur and ammonia routed via the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea. Intensifying West Asia hostilities have, since late FY2025-26, constrained the upstream sulphur/ammonia chain and the downstream FSA byproduct, forcing the Company to disclose a production scale-back to exchanges on 23 May 2026 with a financial impact management calls 'not presently determinable'.
risks.risk: Raw-material (FSA) supply concentration and geopolitical exposure

risks.note: Primary aluminium smelting capacity has consolidated among fewer, larger operators; the largest customer accounted for 69.27% of AlF3 revenue in FY2024-25, up sharply from 52.51% in FY2023-24, while the share from other 10%+ customers (excluding the top two) fell from 20.40% to nil, leaving the Company reliant on a small number of buyers.

The Company manufactures a single product line, Aluminium Fluoride, with no separate segment reporting under Ind AS 108; the ancillary solar power activity is immaterial to revenue and entirely dependent on captive consumption, leaving overall performance tied to one product and its input/output market dynamics.

Demand for AlF3 is transmitted through customers' offtake patterns in the primary aluminium industry, exposing the Company to that industry's cyclicality even though its own qualification-based customer relationships are sticky.
risks.risk: Cyclicality of the primary aluminium industry

risks.note: A portion of the Company's FSA requirement is moved over a longer distance from Odisha, and the associated inland freight cost is absorbed by the Company rather than passed through, an increase in which is flagged as a recurring risk.
The Company is exposed to increases in the cost of fuel, power and consumables, and to foreign-exchange volatility on the limited proportion of imported inputs and capital goods.
risks.risk: Input cost inflation (fuel, power, consumables) and foreign-exchange volatility

risks.note: Management flags the customary risks of fire, environmental incident and industrial accident at its manufacturing operations as a recurring risk category, against which it maintains insurance cover; the Board's overall view is that no material risk threatens the Company's existence.
risks.risk: Operational hazard risk (fire, environmental incident, industrial accident)
